19 January, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 13
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 674 of 2023
Applicant :- Pinku Sharma
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P. Civil Secrett. Lko.

Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.

sentences.text: It is informed by learned A.G.A. that in pursuance of the order of this Court dated 13.01.2023 relevant information has been procured from the concerned police station, moreover, the up-to-date case diary and complete instructions have also been procured for the assistance of this Court.
The information provided by the Police Station Thakurganj, District Lucknow in pursuance of the order of this Court dated 13.01.2023 is taken on record.

Heard Shri Vijay Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Pinku Sharma for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 0396 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Thakurganj,
District Lucknow, during trial.

Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication, even if the allegations, as levelled in the first information report and in the Pinku Sharma vs State Of U.P. sentences.text:
It is further submitted that according to the own version of the victim/prosecutrix they had met in the year 2018, as allegedly the prosecutrix was introduced to the applicant by Rahul with whom the prosecutrix was earlier having relationship and, thereafter, according to the own statement of the prosecutrix, they were regular meeting and cohabiting and in these three years before lodging of the F.I.R. no complaint of any kind has been made by the prosecutrix/victim.
It is further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix is about 26 years, while the age of the instant applicant is about 22 years and, thus, whatever relationship established between the victim and the applicant was a relationship of two adults and the same could not be given the colour of rape.
It is also submitted that in the medical examination of the prosecutrix no injury of any kind or abnormality has been found.
While referring to the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate, it is submitted that the prosecutrix and the instant applicant got married on 23.03.2022.

However, it is stated by victim that subsequent to their marriage the applicant asked her to bring all the jewellery and cash, to which she refused, and thereafter, the applicant asked her to end her life, however, she was saved by her sister and thereafter, a photograph of their marriage was sent by the applicant to her sister-in-law (Bhabhi)
and her father had compromised with the applicant in June, 2022.

In this backdrop, the attention of this Court was also drawn by learned counsel for the applicant towards the Annexure No. 14, which is a photocopy of the compromise allegedly held between the father of the victim and applicant,
wherein the reference of solemnizing court marriage has also been made and a consensus appears to have arrived between the parties not to send any photograph, obscene video, etc. to each other.
Significantly, this compromise has been admitted in the report of the police station taken on record today and also a part of the case diary.

It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 12.11.2022 and he is not having any criminal history and he would co-operate in the investigation as well as in the trial and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that the applicant has committed rape with the victim by blackmailing her and having regard to the seriousness of the offence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the first information report of this case was lodged by the victim herself.

In the F.I.R. as well as in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the allegations are to the tune that it was in the year 2018, the prosecutrix was introduced to the applicant by one Rahul with whom she was earlier having relationship and against whom also the allegation of rape have been levelled and since 2018, they appears to be meeting frequently and were also cohabiting.

However, allegations have Pinku Sharma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P. ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54537486/
2 been levelled by the prosecutrix that such cohabitation was due to the undue influence and pressure applied by the applicant, as he was possessing some photographs, obscene videos of her.

sentences.text: It is an admitted fact that till now no obscene video has been recovered.
However, the investigation is stated to be pending.
The statement of the prosecutrix has already been recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
It has been about two months, the applicant is languishing in jail.
There is nothing on record which may suggest that any effort has been made by the investigating officer to take the accused person on 'police custody remand'.
Even if the charge sheet has not been filed, it appears that the investigation would be at the final stages.

It is submitted with considerable force that it is a case of consent and the prosecutrix is major and there is no material or evidence in support of the allegations levelled by the prosecutrix and at the most, it appears to be a case of 'broken relationship', which according to learned counsel for the applicant has been given the colour of rape.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 12.11.2022 without any criminal antecedents and his presence and co-operation in investigation may be secured by placing adequate conditions.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.
Let the accused/applicant- Pinku Sharma involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) If the investigation of the case is still pending, the applicant shall remain present before the investigating officer as and when required and shall co-operate in the investigation without any excuse.
(ii) The applicant shall not attempt to make contact with the prosecutrix either directly or indirectly or through any social platform or with any of the prosecution witnesses and the violation of these conditions alone shall be a sufficient ground for the trial court to cancel the facility of bail granted by this Court.
(iii) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(iv) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(v) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
